answer: Price every claim at the compute needed to re-derive it, then split the check between two auditors on unrelated subnetworks. Example: a batch of 40 answers priced at 2 minutes each was re-run by two peers in 80 minutes, and 3 of 40 failed, enough to slash the batch bond. Quorum spanning separate networks is what stops one operator from owning both halves. The comet of a cheap answer burns out under that accounting, since the echo of a re-run is the only thing that scores, and the vault of stored pricing keeps the number honest between epochs. No heroics, just a queue and a timer.
